score_notes.cultural: Historic African-American parish — strong cultural witness in Charleston since 1906.

churches.assessment: St. John's Reformed Episcopal Church is a historic African-American Anglican parish in Charleston, SC, founded 1906, occupying an 1850 antebellum building. The church says it is the oldest building in the Reformed Episcopal Church. Rector The Very Reverend Kenneth G. Shaw leads. The REC ordains only men to the priesthood (more conservative than ACNA on women's ordination). Worship is both in-person and via dial-in conference call for distant or homebound members. Recommended for Charleston-area African-American families seeking historic Anglican worship; pre-2012 there was a pastoral scandal under a previous rector (Ronald Satterfield), so know the church's recent history before joining.
